info.what: First review of an alert, using the alert, the customer profile and recent activity.
info.when: Choose this to practise deciding quickly whether an alert can be closed or needs a closer look.
info.mistake: Trying to prove the crime. At this level you only need to decide whether the alert is explained.

info.what: Ends the review because the activity is explained by what you can see.
info.when: Use it when the facts in the case explain why the alert was raised.
info.mistake: Closing because the amount seems small, without recording what explains the activity.

info.what: Sends the case to a Level 2 investigator, with your short note.
info.when: Use it when the activity remains unexplained or the warning signs need deeper review.
info.mistake: Escalating everything to be safe, or escalating without saying what concerned you.

info.what: Full review of an escalated case, including documents, connected parties and a guided report.
info.when: Choose this to practise testing a suspicion and explaining it to the {nominatedShort}.
info.mistake: Repeating the earlier analyst's notes without checking the underlying facts.

info.what: Ends the investigation because the evidence explains the activity.
info.when: Use it when the evidence you gathered removes the concern.
info.mistake: Closing on the customer's explanation alone when it can be checked against documents.

info.what: Sends your internal report to the {nominated}, who decides whether a {report} is made.
info.when: Use it when you know or suspect money laundering or terrorist financing after your review.
info.mistake: Waiting for proof. A suspicion is enough for the internal report.

info.what: Final review of a referred case, including the quality of the work done before it reached you.
info.when: Choose this to practise deciding whether a {report} should be sent to the {fiuShort}.
info.mistake: Accepting the referral as written without testing its reasoning.

info.what: Records a reasoned decision that no {report} will be made.
info.when: Use it when the referral does not support knowledge or suspicion after your review.
Use it when the referral supports knowledge or suspicion and the report is complete.
info.mistake: Filing a report that does not say why the activity is suspicious.
